places.name: Senso-ji Temple
places.description: Tokyo's oldest and most visited temple, in the historic Asakusa district, reached through the iconic Kaminarimon Gate and a bustling shopping street of traditional snacks and souvenirs.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing & Center Gai
places.description: The world's busiest pedestrian intersection, surrounded by neon billboards, department stores, and the famous Hachiko statue — the defining image of modern Tokyo.

places.name: Meiji Shrine & Yoyogi Park
places.description: A serene Shinto shrine set within a forested park near Harajuku, offering a tranquil escape from the city and a glimpse of traditional Japanese ceremony and architecture.

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.description: A lively food market of narrow lanes lined with stalls selling fresh sushi, street snacks, and kitchenware — the best place in the city to sample Tokyo's seafood culture.

places.name: TeamLab Planets / Odaiba
places.description: An immersive digital art museum of light and water installations, part of Tokyo's futuristic Odaiba waterfront district known for its shopping malls and bay views.

places.name: Osaka Castle
places.description: A reconstructed 16th-century castle set in a large park famous for cherry blossoms, with a museum inside chronicling the life of its original builder, Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

places.name: Dotonbori
places.description: Osaka's iconic canal-side entertainment district, ablaze with neon signs and giant illuminated billboards, and the heart of the city's street food scene — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and kushikatsu.

places.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
places.description: A 190-stall covered market known as 'Osaka's Kitchen,' where visitors can sample fresh seafood, wagyu skewers, and seasonal produce straight from the vendors.

places.name: Umeda Sky Building
places.description: A striking twin-tower skyscraper connected by a 'floating garden' observatory on its roof, offering 360-degree views over Osaka's skyline, especially striking at sunset.

places.name: Shitennoji Temple
places.description: One of Japan's oldest Buddhist temples, founded in 593 AD, with a five-story pagoda, peaceful gardens, and a lively flea market held on the 21st and 22nd of each month.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
places.description: A famous Shinto shrine at the base of a mountain, known for its thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up wooded trails dotted with smaller shrines and fox statues.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
places.description: A Zen Buddhist temple whose top two floors are completely covered in gold leaf, reflected dramatically in the still pond of its surrounding strolling garden.

places.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
places.description: A towering bamboo forest path on Kyoto's western edge, near the Tenryu-ji temple gardens and the Togetsukyo Bridge over the Katsura River.

places.name: Gion District
places.description: Kyoto's famous geisha district, with preserved wooden machiya townhouses, traditional teahouses, and a chance — at dusk — to spot a geiko or maiko on her way to an appointment.

places.name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
places.description: A UNESCO World Heritage temple built on a hillside without a single nail, famous for its wooden stage offering sweeping views over Kyoto and the surrounding maple and cherry trees.

places.name: Fukuoka Castle Ruins & Maizuru Park
places.description: The stone foundations of a 17th-century castle set within a park famous for cherry blossoms, offering panoramic views over the city and Hakata Bay.

places.name: Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine
places.description: A revered Shinto shrine dedicated to the god of learning, set among thousands of plum trees, and one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Kyushu.

places.name: Yatai Food Stalls (Nakasu & Tenjin)
places.description: Fukuoka's famous open-air street food stalls that line the riverbanks at night, serving the city's signature tonkotsu ramen, yakitori, and oden in a convivial, communal setting.

places.name: Ohori Park
places.description: A large central park built around a lake modeled on West Lake in Hangzhou, with a Japanese garden, walking paths, and the Fukuoka Art Museum on its grounds.

places.name: Canal City Hakata
places.description: A sprawling shopping and entertainment complex built around an artificial canal, with theaters, a cinema, fountains, and a wide range of dining and retail.
